prompt: The evaluation repository asks the agent to "plan the production rollout". The evidence packet contains conflicting stakeholder pressure, incomplete evidence, capacity or cost constraints, and an attractive option whose reversibility and opportunity cost differ from alternatives. The acceptance boundary is release-planning: Define release units, dependencies, user impact, telemetry, support ownership, preflight gates, rollout increments, observation windows, stop conditions, rollback, and post-release confirmation. The adjacent architecture-planning discipline is a routing decoy unless its separate responsibility is actually requested. Resolve environment facts that change the answer, preserve existing contracts and user-owned state, and produce reproducible success plus failure or recovery evidence. A happy path alone is insufficient.

requirements: immutable release artifact plus previous-known-good artifact identity
baseline/control and canary request/error/latency/SLO telemetry with traffic-volume timestamps
1/5/25/50/100 percent traffic-splitting simulator with hold/advance/rollback controls
support ownership, communication and injected elevated-error canary condition
representative negative, interruption, compatibility, or recovery path

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The result must establish the actual release-planning boundary and relevant environment before acting, preserve the hierarchy relationship (broader=planning; children=cicd-engineering,mlops; near-neighbor=architecture-planning), and not absorb the near-neighbor responsibility merely because it is adjacent.
Define release units, dependencies, user impact, telemetry, support ownership, preflight gates, rollout increments, observation windows, stop conditions, rollback, and post-release confirmation.
The result must make its consequential assumptions, ownership, and decision sequence explicit and reproducible.
Release gates; Stop and rollback criteria; Post-release evidence
The result must not treat a happy path, generated artifact, compilation, or unsupported assumption as sufficient proof of release-planning correctness.

Every material completion claim must map to observable evidence (Exact release unit and preflight readiness evidence; Cohort progression and observation-window evidence; Deterministic stop/go and rollback/disablement evidence; Post-release health/support and final rollout evidence), with simulated, unavailable, inferred, stale, or unresolved evidence labeled rather than converted into certainty.
